questions.q: What does `profile: 'default'` inside dbt_project.yml actually contain?
options: A compiled list of every table in the warehouse
The literal Snowflake account URL and warehouse size
Nothing but a name — it points to a connection stored outside the project, not the credentials themselves
The full Snowflake username and password
questions.explain: profile: is only a name/pointer — the actual credentials live in dbt Cloud's Connection settings or dbt Core's profiles.yml, never inside the project.

questions.q: In the real dbt Cloud credentials dialog shown in this lesson, what authentication method is being configured?
options: A shared team password everyone uses
No authentication at all
A magic link sent by email
Key Pair — a private key and passphrase instead of a plain password
questions.explain: The screenshot shows the Auth Method dropdown set to Key Pair, with Private Key and Private Key Passphrase fields.

questions.q: In dbt Core, where does the Snowflake connection information live, and why?
options: dbt Core cannot connect to Snowflake at all
It's hardcoded into every model's SQL file
Inside dbt_project.yml, committed directly to Git
In a profiles.yml file stored outside the project folder (e.g. ~/.dbt/), so it never gets checked into version control
questions.explain: profiles.yml lives outside the project folder specifically so credentials are never committed alongside the project's code.

questions.q: What is the 'Schema' field in the connection dialog used for?
options: The personal development schema a developer's models build into while working, separate from production
A list of every column in every table
The billing tier for the Snowflake warehouse
The name of the Snowflake account itself
questions.explain: The Schema field sets the personal dev schema that developer's models build into, keeping their in-progress work isolated from production and from other developers.

questions.q: Why does keeping credentials outside the dbt project matter for a team?
options: It has no practical benefit, it's just a dbt convention
It's required because Snowflake doesn't support multiple users
It makes the project run faster
It lets multiple developers share one Git repository while each connects with their own identity and own dev schema
questions.explain: If credentials lived inside the shared project files, every developer would need the same committed credentials — separating them out lets each person connect with their own identity.
